lantern_han_tao.name: Han Tao
lantern_han_tao.title: Vegetable seller
lantern_han_tao.description: A seller balancing family duties with the ordinary costs of her stall.

lantern_lan_de.name: Lan De
lantern_lan_de.title: Roofer
lantern_lan_de.description: A roofer recovering with qualified care after an ordinary work accident.

lantern_pu_mei.name: Pu Mei
lantern_pu_mei.title: School pupil
lantern_pu_mei.description: Pu An's daughter, author of a school account about a toy volcano.

lantern_hou_zhen.name: Hou Zhen
lantern_hou_zhen.title: Association clerk
lantern_hou_zhen.description: The received successor to a finite documentary term.

lantern_08_001.speaker: narrator
lantern_08_001.text: Day 1465 began with a broken egg on the stair. Yu Ming had carried her breakfast too close to the rail, where the carpenter had left a projecting nail. She stood over the yellow patch looking exhausted beyond anything an egg warranted. Yue brought a rag. Neither woman called the accident a lesson. They cleaned it, bought another egg from the woman downstairs, and ate sitting on the landing. Yu had spent her examination evening serving dinner to customers who knew nothing of the effort behind her ordinary bowl.

lantern_08_002.speaker: narrator
lantern_08_002.text: At the yard Shao declined to open the second cabinet. The first course had used its four reference cells, and the next appointment was presently a conversation. Yue had brought the plan she had drawn after the concert: preparation along one route, release, a rest interval, then a second route under a different ordinary disturbance. It was a useful plan. Shao put her finger on the blank place where the paid observer should stand. Good handwriting did not supply that person, or the charge that person would have to verify.

lantern_08_003.speaker: narrator
lantern_08_003.text: Gao Fen was already outside, leaning against the warm brick. His kiln had offered him an extra firing shift. Accepting it would pay for his next inspection but leave no recovery day before the appointment. He wanted Shao to move his appointment, although the published small grant had a closing date. Yue expected an argument about priorities. Instead Shao took the appointment book to the grant clerk and asked whether its date rule allowed an ordinary postponement for documented work. Gao followed her. His request belonged to him.

lantern_08_004.speaker: narrator
lantern_08_004.text: The answer took two days. During those days Gao worked the shift, and Yue attended no live session. The six-copper grant remained conditional, rather than becoming an unofficial loan from the relay cabinet. At the inn, Gao described the kiln's new apprentice dropping a load of pale tiles into the sand. He was angry because he had spent the afternoon salvaging them, and proud because the apprentice had admitted what happened before anyone stepped on a sharp edge. A person could feel both things without resolving either into a speech.

lantern_08_005.speaker: narrator
lantern_08_005.text: Yue's next wages were easier to settle. Deng Si checked the twenty completed calendar days of the second documentary term, including its agreed weekly rest days, and released seventy-five copper on account of the contracted one hundred fifty. The remaining seventy-five stayed payable when the term ended on Day 1475. This was part payment for work already received, not a new allowance. Yue put it into her purse beside the money she had actually retained. For the first time that week, a course price was a possible choice rather than a wish.

lantern_08_006.speaker: narrator
lantern_08_006.text: The extension offered six two-hour appointments for twenty-four copper and a separate sixteen-copper bench budget: six compatible reference cells at two copper each, plus four for their intake and final inspection. Shao would not call the inspection free simply because she stood in the same yard for other pupils. She showed her the priced sheet and the available dates. The six appointments covered preparation and interruption practice, not a certificate or an unlimited right to repeat. A failed session could consume its charge and still require a later fee.

lantern_08_007.speaker: narrator
lantern_08_007.text: Yue paid forty copper on Day 1467. She left enough of the received wages for the contracted room and ordinary meals until her next settlement, rather than buying the attractive cloth Rui Sui had brought to town. Rui put the cloth away without pretending not to be disappointed. The order would have paid part of her own journey home. They talked through the disappointment directly, over the table where the unopened parcel lay. Friendship gave Rui someone who listened; it did not convert Yue's purse into a compulsory purchase.

lantern_08_008.speaker: narrator
lantern_08_008.text: The reference cells arrived on Day 1468 in a smaller box than Yue expected. Shao and the paid inspector opened it in daylight, checked each numbered seal, and rejected one scratched contact before it entered the accepted tray. The seller replaced that unit under the same purchase before the first session. Six accepted cells remained six accepted cells. The scratched unit went back marked for inspection, its possible charge unavailable to their course. Yue watched how little drama surrounded a refusal that might have become dramatic if someone had first promised a demonstration.

lantern_08_009.speaker: narrator
lantern_08_009.text: Their first appointment, on Day 1469, used no live circuit. Shao asked Yue to explain the ordinary route from the lower reservoir through the prepared primary channels and back to full grounded release. Twelve primary channels meant six pairs, however tempting the picture of eight spokes might look on her page. She changed the diagram she had made too symmetrical. The correction mattered because she had been imagining a pause at an invented junction. When she described the actual turn correctly, it felt less elegant and more navigable.

lantern_08_010.speaker: narrator
lantern_08_010.text: Shao placed three wooden markers on the practice table. One indicated a breath interrupted by speech, another the arrival of a messenger, and the third a physical movement that Yue herself chose. None was a command to continue. She had to show where she would cease input, where a prepared route would remain unfinished, and how she would complete an ordinary release before answering the person. She moved the markers after her first explanation. Learning one favorable order would teach her the arrangement of the table rather than the work.

lantern_08_011.speaker: narrator
lantern_08_011.text: At her documentary shift that afternoon, an actual messenger interrupted her count. Yue put down the pen and finished the tally mark before looking up. The messenger was twelve and impatient, carrying a cancellation from Moss Ford. He wanted a stamp quickly because his brother had a boat to catch. Yue read the line that canceled the afternoon window, then asked which boat. It was the last passenger crossing before a bank inspection. She passed the received notice to the operator and let the boy leave with the stamped copy.

lantern_08_012.speaker: narrator
lantern_08_012.text: The cancellation did not stay on her desk. Moss Ford's receiving operator had fever, and the named relief worker was already covering a different settlement. Their accepted rota contained no spare person that afternoon. Deng moved the message to the ground dispatch, which would arrive the next day. An older merchant shouted that the tower itself was healthy. Yue looked up at the lit housing and understood why he shouted. Its visible health made the absent receiver feel like a deliberate insult, although no light could make a sick person work safely.

lantern_08_013.speaker: narrator
lantern_08_013.text: Wen Shun was among the people waiting. He had come early this time and carried his wage sheet in a cover that kept the ink dry. When Deng announced the cancellation, Wen laughed once, without humor. Yue did not tell him that his punctuality was still worthwhile. He knew that. She helped him find the actual ground departure and its expected arrival, then left him to decide whether the delay changed his purchase. He chose not to send the instruction. The grain he meant to buy would have gone by then.

lantern_08_014.speaker: narrator
lantern_08_014.text: By the evening, several traders were arguing over a petition demanding that every receiving station employ a permanent second operator. Their desired service was reasonable. Its funding was not presently in the association's accepted term. Pu An sat down with them and worked out what a second full post, relief, and housing would cost, rather than reducing the request to a scolding about impatience. The amount surprised even the petition's author. They still signed it. A petition could ask the six institutions to choose a different budget next year without purchasing that budget today.

lantern_08_015.speaker: narrator
lantern_08_015.text: At home Pu's daughter, Pu Mei, found the second volcano lid sitting beside his tools. She turned it over and said its underside was uglier than the first. The first had jammed, and this one lifted properly. Pu asked whether she wanted an explanation of the clearance. She wanted to paint it red. He brought out the paint, remembering to ask the landlady before they spread paper across the floor. Yue watched their serious argument about the shade of lava while trying not to smile at either person's entirely different standard of success.

lantern_08_016.speaker: narrator
lantern_08_016.text: On Day 1470 Yue's ordinary recovery check after the dry appointment found no new tissue symptoms. The visit belonged to the paid extension even though the previous day had used explanation rather than charge. Shao reviewed sleep, meals, and the actual four-hour job. Yue had slept poorly because the upstairs child cried through the night. She moved the next live appointment from morning to afternoon, after a permitted rest period, without adding another live attempt. The child's distress did not become an examination obstacle for someone else to overcome heroically.

lantern_08_017.speaker: narrator
lantern_08_017.text: Yue asked the child's mother whether anything was needed downstairs. Tian Rui wanted someone to collect the mended carrying strap from the cobbler while she stayed with her son. Yue collected it after her shift. The cobbler had used a leather offcut; the repair was visible and strong. Tian paid him herself when he came for his basket in the evening. Her son gripped the strap and refused to let anyone lift the basket. They let him hold it empty, an accommodation that improved the room more quickly than an argument.

lantern_08_018.speaker: narrator
lantern_08_018.text: Day 1472's practice began after ordinary work, a meal, and rest. Shao measured the prepared reference stock and Yue's current usable reserve through the accepted sampling procedure before allowing the named short route. The live input remained half a unit across four ordinary breaths, with no breath receiving more than one eighth. Useful output remained a quarter unit at the old fixture. Yue was practicing the control and return path around that bounded activity. A larger diagram did not make the fixture capable of a larger discharge.

lantern_08_019.speaker: narrator
lantern_08_019.text: Shao spoke while she began the third breath. She asked a question about the messenger she had helped, and she almost answered before ceasing input. The movement caught her attention in time. She stopped at the agreed point, completed grounded release, and spoke only after the fixture's indicator was quiet. The route had not reached its intended second prepared segment. Shao recorded an interrupted practice, not a failed certificate trial and not a completed circuit. Yue's answer about the messenger was accurate, which did nothing to alter the unfinished route.

lantern_08_020.speaker: narrator
lantern_08_020.text: The useful lesson appeared in the next repetition, conducted within the same funded session after its specified rest. Yue could not count on recognizing every interruption by its subject. Shao asked about the weather, and she stopped just as deliberately. The accepted cell supported the session's bounded reference activity, with the actual draw recorded. They did not divide its remaining indication into an imaginary extra cell. At the close, the cell was marked spent for this course, and the fixture was cold before either person gathered the papers.

lantern_08_021.speaker: narrator
lantern_08_021.text: Day 1473's following check found ordinary sensation, strength, and movement, with no new localized pain. Yue had still taken the night to recover. She could feel pleased with the stop without treating the absence of injury as permission to repeat indefinitely. Shao gave her the corrected route page and asked her to put it away for the afternoon. She went to the riverside laundry instead. The women there were disputing who had borrowed a copper pin, a mystery whose resolution required asking Pu Mei rather than further introspection.

lantern_08_022.speaker: narrator
lantern_08_022.text: Pu Mei had made the pin into a flagpole for the volcano. She returned it when the owner asked, with a strip of red cloth still tied to its head. Pu apologized for not recognizing the pin at breakfast and bought his daughter a plain wooden skewer of her own. Yue liked the visible ending of this small dispute: the pin returned, the apology addressed to its owner, the replacement in the child's hand. Nobody needed the volcano to become a public moral performance. It needed a flagpole that belonged to it.

lantern_08_023.speaker: narrator
lantern_08_023.text: At the relay, An Shou proposed marking the canceled Moss Ford window as a completed opportunity because Chime had staffed its side. Deng refused the wording. Chime's staff had been present and should be paid; the intended exchange had still not occurred. Both facts belonged in the record. An was worried that the grant office would treat a cancellation as proof his counters were unnecessary. He admitted that fear after the room emptied. Deng agreed to carry the staffing evidence separately, rather than hiding the lost service inside a more flattering total.

lantern_08_024.speaker: narrator
lantern_08_024.text: Yue helped An write the two statements. The first named the actual staffing and its contracted cost. The second named the lost window, the fever, and the unavailable relief. Combining them into one success count would have made the petition for better staffing harder to understand. An reread the page twice before signing. It was one thing to accept an accurate correction when a clerk pointed at arithmetic. It was another to let a report accurately describe a weakness that might influence whether one's next employment term existed.

lantern_08_025.speaker: narrator
lantern_08_025.text: Her own term ended on Day 1475 with the files where the successor could find them. Deng paid the remaining seventy-five copper, bringing the completed thirty calendar days to the contracted one hundred fifty. The wages included the agreed rest arrangement and did not purchase more days after the term. Yue left a note about An's two-part reporting change, returned the borrowed key, and ate a late lunch with the room's paid staff. A bowl cracked while they washed up. The lunch remained enjoyable, and the cupboard lost a bowl.

lantern_08_026.speaker: narrator
lantern_08_026.text: The successor was a quiet local clerk named Hou Zhen, appointed by the association for its remaining documentary work from a separate administrative allocation approved by its members. Yue did not train him indefinitely out of friendship. The handover had occupied her final paid shift; a later question would either be brief ordinary conversation or a newly accepted task. Hou found one index label unclear and asked before she left. They corrected it together. The correction saved him an afternoon without turning him into a pupil obligated to repeat her preferences.

lantern_08_027.speaker: narrator
lantern_08_027.text: Unemployed was too broad a word for the next morning, and employed was false. Yue had booked appointments, a paid room, a small purse, and time in which to look for the next job. At the market she met a school copyist named He Pu, who wanted twenty-four short reading sheets reproduced from his own corrected originals. The work paid two copper per accepted sheet, with errors returned for repair before acceptance. Delivery was spread across sixteen days. He needed someone who could copy clearly and stop arguing with the original.

lantern_08_028.speaker: narrator
lantern_08_028.text: Yue looked at the originals before agreeing. Several were children's accounts of ordinary journeys, edited with their families' permission for the school. One was by Pu Mei, describing a volcano that erupted in a basin because her father worried about the floor. He Pu had added a comma that made the sentence funnier and much harder to copy without laughing. Yue accepted the forty-eight-copper contract on Day 1476. The school's already collected materials fund would pay on accepted batches. The relay association's fuel and operator budget did not enter the agreement.

lantern_08_029.speaker: narrator
lantern_08_029.text: The contract allowed her to copy at home, around the existing appointments, but did not let her lend the children's originals to a paying publisher. Rui asked whether she could show a particularly charming account to a buyer interested in illustrated cloth. Yue asked He Pu instead of quietly agreeing. He said the classroom consent did not cover a commercial design. Rui accepted the answer and approached the child's parent with her own proposal through the school. The possible sale now had a person who could decide whether it should happen.

lantern_08_030.speaker: narrator
lantern_08_030.text: On Day 1477 Yue's second live session introduced a deliberate movement interruption. She prepared a short circuit segment, began the bounded input, and at Shao's sign lifted her heel as though stepping away from the table. The motion broke the rhythm earlier than her written plan predicted. She stopped input, released, and put her foot down without trying to preserve the elegant count. Shao asked her to locate the difference in the plan. The page assumed she would move at the end of a breath. Her body had started midway through one.

lantern_08_031.speaker: narrator
lantern_08_031.text: They repeated the explanation dry, changing the movement's timing. Yue drew no new junction to make the discrepancy disappear. She marked the route's actual incomplete portion and the return she had used. Her reserve reading after that day's specified activity and sampling was higher than her arrival baseline, but still below eighty-four actually usable units. Shao wrote the measured seventy-four and five eighths beside the day, not beside a title promising great-circuit certification. This practice taught control inside the capacity she presently possessed. It did not reward successful stopping with invisible extra charge.

lantern_08_032.speaker: narrator
lantern_08_032.text: The following Day 1478 check found no altered strength or sensation. Yue nevertheless spent most of it copying at a lower table because her back was stiff from sitting badly the previous evening. Shao distinguished the ordinary postural ache from the examined routes without dismissing the ache itself. Pu brought an older chair he owned, whose back supported her better, and took the ill-fitting chair away for his own bench. The exchange solved a practical problem. Yue did not suddenly acquire a stronger spine from being correctly examined.

lantern_08_033.speaker: narrator
lantern_08_033.text: Day 1479's six accepted sheets earned twelve copper. He Pu returned a seventh because she had copied a crossed-out word that was not meant to appear. She repaired it without charging twice, then laughed when he showed her how many times he had nearly made the same error preparing the original. She spent part of the received money on food and set the rest beside the future room charge. A contract total could help her plan, but an unaccepted sheet could not yet buy supper from someone who expected coins.

lantern_08_034.speaker: narrator
lantern_08_034.text: Ma visited after her relief shift carrying news of the staffing petition. Alder Reach supported funding an additional trained receiver next year. Ring Meadow wanted a cheaper rotating arrangement. East Sill asked for the actual missed-message count before voting. None had promised immediate personnel. Ma thought Ring Meadow's plan would fail because it treated travel days as if they were shifts at a desk. Yue asked whether she had written that experience into the consultation. Ma had been angry enough to talk about it at dinner and tired enough not to write it.

lantern_08_035.speaker: narrator
lantern_08_035.text: They worked on Ma's statement after eating. Yue did not put institutional language into Ma's mouth. She asked when Ma had traveled, when she had recovered, and which roster entry had expected her in two places. Ma supplied the dates and crossed out a sentence that sounded as though she never wanted to relieve another station. She did want the work, paid and arranged so that it could occur. The statement went under Ma's name, with Yue acknowledged only as the person who copied the finished version clearly.

lantern_08_036.speaker: narrator
lantern_08_036.text: The third appointment, on Day 1480, was an ordinary release drill after a longer prepared approach. Yue completed neither a full great circuit nor an examination threshold. Shao introduced a pause at a point that would tempt her to hold input while deciding what to do next. She ceased it instead. The indicator showed the planned release, and the next ordinary breath remained unforced. She remembered the marsh's argument about seeing a favorable trace and wishing it lasted. Here a shorter trace was precisely the evidence of the action she intended.

lantern_08_037.speaker: narrator
lantern_08_037.text: Yue had also begun mistaking anticipation for knowledge. Before the marker moved, she wanted to stop because she suspected Shao would interrupt her. She explained that a controlled interruption required a route actually begun under the named conditions. Refusing every activity could avoid its failure while teaching nothing about release from it. They used the remaining paid session for dry distinctions between not beginning, beginning and stopping, and finishing the bounded old task. No one awarded her a completed live route for explaining those distinctions neatly.

lantern_08_038.speaker: narrator
lantern_08_038.text: At the next-day check on Day 1481, the expected tissues were ordinary. The dry work had also left Yue tired of her own explanations. She invited Yu Ming to walk to the bank where the laundresses dried linen. Yu brought two buns and refused to discuss anyone's reserve. A boy had tied a paper bird to a line above the water. When the wind stopped, it hung upside down. They sat watching it become briefly graceful and then ridiculous again, without agreeing that it represented their current lives.

lantern_08_039.speaker: narrator
lantern_08_039.text: On the same afternoon Zheng Lin lost the cane's new sleeve between his room and the plaza. His niece found it by the baker's doorway, already stepped on and split. He wanted to insist that the maker had fitted it poorly. She reminded him that he had pulled it loose while demonstrating an older workshop grip to a visitor. He admitted this reluctantly. The lost sleeve could be replaced for a price; the time they spent circling the plaza could not be returned to the lesson he had hoped to teach.

lantern_08_040.speaker: narrator
lantern_08_040.text: Yue accompanied them to Pu's bench, where Zheng paid for a plain replacement and declined a decorative cap. Pu asked whether the older man needed a wider handle rather than another sleeve. Zheng answered sharply before trying the borrowed sample. It rested better against his palm. He ordered one and still complained about how ugly it was. Yue was glad that neither gratitude nor age had made him agreeable. His body needed a better handle, and his niece needed an uncle who could accept it without making her earn every inch of help.

lantern_08_041.speaker: narrator
lantern_08_041.text: The fourth appointment's date had been set for Day 1482. A roofing accident at the neighboring dye shop sent the paid observer to an actual emergency that morning. Shao postponed the live session. The observer was a qualified carer whose emergency rota took precedence under the disclosed booking; her alternate had already accepted another task. Yue did not prefer a curriculum where the clinic ignored an injured roofer. She also did not enjoy losing the prepared afternoon. Shao offered the later available date without pretending the disappointment made her impatient in a shameful way.

lantern_08_042.speaker: narrator
lantern_08_042.text: The roofer, Lan De, had fallen only a short distance and injured his wrist badly enough that his ordinary work changed. He Pu asked Yue whether she could add a larger copying batch because the school caretaker would now need paid help with physical repairs. Yue could copy but could not inspect a broken roof or fund an undefined replacement worker. She accepted four additional reading sheets at the existing rate, payable separately from the school's remaining approved materials money. The sum was eight copper, not an imagined rescue of the whole school.

lantern_08_043.speaker: narrator
lantern_08_043.text: The original forty-eight-copper contract and the eight-copper addition together required twenty-eight accepted sheets. Yue wrote that count on the room wall where she would not mix it with relay windows or practice appointments. Pu Mei's volcano account was one of them, and her mother objected to a copied drawing that made the smoke look like a monster. The drawing had been He Pu's addition. He removed it before the next batch. A child's accepted words did not mean every adult illustration could travel under the same quiet approval.

lantern_08_044.speaker: narrator
lantern_08_044.text: Gao Fen returned to the yard on Day 1483 with the grant clerk's amendment in writing. The allowed appointment date had moved, his kiln wages had been paid, and he could resume his own bounded preparation. He had not performed Yue's missing session in the meantime. Shao reviewed his particular clinical restrictions and reserved a different fixture interval. Yue congratulated him on getting the date changed. Gao said the relief mattered more than congratulations. Then he asked whether Yue would help carry a bag of meal to his room after both had finished.

lantern_08_045.speaker: narrator
lantern_08_045.text: They walked home slowly because Gao had already worked that morning. He told Yue about the apprentice's first intact tile batch and the supervisor who wanted to call it his own improved training. Gao had corrected him in front of the apprentice. The correction might cost him a pleasant assignment later. Yue offered no prediction that honesty would certainly be rewarded. She asked whether the apprentice had heard. Gao had seen him straighten. That was an actual consequence, smaller than a repaired hierarchy and large enough to matter to him.

lantern_08_046.speaker: narrator
lantern_08_046.text: The evening brought an unexpected letter from Rui. The child's parent had declined the cloth illustration proposal, but another family had accepted a separate design based on their own orchard account under a priced, bounded agreement. Rui had not lost the whole journey's purpose when one proposal failed. Yue laid the letter beside her accepted sheets and felt the distinction between asking for a relationship and assuming it owed her a use. Rui's next visit would involve another family's chosen drawing. Pu Mei's volcano would remain on the school page.

lantern_08_047.speaker: narrator
lantern_08_047.text: Deng sent word that the next year's staffing discussion would continue after the relay's scheduled retirement assessment. This year's three-window service still had its term and its physically aging housing. New appointments could not be advertised as though a petition had restored the lost evening. The announcement disappointed the merchants who had organized around visible light. Yue heard their argument outside the noodle stall and walked past without becoming the association's unpaid spokeswoman. Her received work had ended. She could be a resident listening to a discussion that concerned her.

lantern_08_048.speaker: narrator
lantern_08_048.text: One incident from the walk with Yu kept returning to Yue. At the bank they had met an older sister scolding a younger brother for throwing a pebble at the paper bird. He said it had already been broken. The sister untied the line and showed him the puncture. Being disappointed in the way a thing flew did not make it ownerless. Yu helped them tape the tear with the paste she carried for sealing food labels. The bird flew lower afterward. Its earlier height was gone, and the boy could see the change.

lantern_08_049.speaker: narrator
lantern_08_049.text: The sister, Han Tao, sold washed vegetables and had built the bird to keep her brother occupied during the stall's quiet hours. She asked Yu whether labels with better paste would survive the damp baskets. Yu offered the maker's address rather than her restaurant's entire packet. They had paid for that packet to label food already sold. Han went to the maker the following morning and ordered a small batch. Her brother carried the repaired bird tucked under his arm. He had been permitted to keep it, with the puncture still showing.

lantern_08_050.speaker: narrator
lantern_08_050.text: Yue bought greens from Han later in the week. The new label on the basket named the harvest day, which mattered more to her than its tidy lettering. Han said several customers had preferred the unmarked baskets because they could bargain by claiming everything looked old. Marking the day had not increased every sale. It had made a different kind of dispute possible. Yue chose the fresh greens and paid the posted amount. An improvement did not need universal applause to be something its maker wanted to continue.

lantern_08_051.speaker: narrator
lantern_08_051.text: That purchase became dinner with Tian Rui and her son. Tian had returned to carrying lighter garments while another worker took the heavier bundles under a separate accepted rate. Her income had fallen for the week. She was glad of the lighter work and worried about the income, which Yue could understand without claiming their courses were alike. The child ate three greens and announced that this was many. Yue considered telling him the vegetable seller's story. Tian shook her head gently. He needed to eat, and the adults could talk afterward.

lantern_08_052.speaker: narrator
lantern_08_052.text: When he slept, Tian asked about the copying job. She could write carefully and hoped to earn at home during wet weather. Yue showed her He Pu's public notice for substitute copyists, not the children's originals that happened to be on her desk. Tian applied with an ordinary handwriting sample of her own. He Pu accepted her for a separate six-sheet batch when another copyist declined the dates. Yue had introduced an opportunity, not employed a dependent. Tian's agreed price and acceptance belonged to the school and to Tian.

lantern_08_053.speaker: narrator
lantern_08_053.text: Tian's first rejected sheet upset her more than Yue had expected. She had omitted a line and feared He Pu would cancel the whole batch. He pointed to the repair provision and returned only that sheet. Yue lent her the better chair for an evening while sitting on a stool to mend her sleeve. By bedtime the line was restored and the page recopied. Tian brought the chair back in the morning. They had solved a particular evening's difficulty. Neither woman had promised that the other could always supply furniture, confidence, or time.

lantern_08_054.speaker: narrator
lantern_08_054.text: The school caretaker visited the room to collect its accepted copies. Lan De had been given paid leave under the roof contractor's existing accident agreement, but the school's roof itself still needed a different licensed worker. He Pu had obtained two quotes and chosen a bounded patch, leaving a larger replacement for the school's later decision. The caretaker showed Yue the temporary closure notice for the wet classroom. Children moved to the covered courtyard for three mornings. They lost quiet and desk space, and the teacher changed the lessons accordingly.

lantern_08_055.speaker: narrator
lantern_08_055.text: Pu Mei hated the courtyard lessons because older pupils could hear her reading. Pu offered to practice the account with her at home. She did not want to read the volcano story to him again; he already knew where to laugh. Yue listened instead and accidentally laughed at the wrong place. Pu Mei glared, then explained that the funny sentence was the next one. Yue listened again. The second reading went better. By the following morning the child had decided that being heard might be tolerable if people waited for the actual joke.

lantern_08_056.speaker: narrator
lantern_08_056.text: Her classroom reading still stumbled. An older boy interrupted before the punch line, and Pu Mei stopped rather than speaking louder. The teacher asked the boy to wait and let her begin the sentence again. She finished, got the laugh where she wanted it, and refused to repeat the account at lunch. Yue heard this from her father, whose pride made the interruption disappear in the first version. Pu Mei restored it when she joined them. She wanted him pleased with what had happened, rather than with an easier performance she had never given.

lantern_08_057.speaker: narrator
lantern_08_057.text: At the dye shop the roofer's younger helper came to collect his tools. Several were borrowed from another crew, which needed them the next day. Lan De could not carry the heavier bag with his injured wrist. The helper fetched it under the foreman's written collection instruction and returned the borrowed pieces before storing the rest. The accident had not made every tool a collective emergency resource. Returning them also meant the original crew could complete its own accepted repair, instead of becoming another delayed job inside a story about helping someone.

lantern_08_058.speaker: narrator
lantern_08_058.text: Yue met the helper at the bakery, where he was choosing bread with the small collection wage he had actually received. He complained that the foreman had described him as merely available. He had missed a fishing afternoon with his friends. Yue asked whether the agreed wage included that change in plans. It did; he had accepted the task and still regretted the afternoon. She was learning how often a chosen, adequately paid piece of work could leave a person grumbling for reasons that were neither evidence of coercion nor a bill for another person.

lantern_08_059.speaker: narrator
lantern_08_059.text: On the evening of Day 1483, He Pu accepted another six original sheets and the repaired seventh, paying fourteen copper for those seven accepted copies. Alongside the first twelve, Yue had now received twenty-six against the original forty-eight-copper batch, leaving eleven original sheets and the four-sheet addition to be accepted later. She could explain the balance because it determined next week's room payment. She did not recopy the figures into her cultivation notebook. The money and the practice had different uses, even when one helped make the other possible.

lantern_08_060.speaker: narrator
lantern_08_060.text: Shao sent a short message confirming the postponed appointment on Day 1486, with the following check on Day 1487. The later dates remained subject to actual recovery, and the booking did not extend into a great-circuit examination. Yue put the message beside the remaining copying work and rearranged two afternoons, leaving time to eat between jobs. The arrangement was less inspiring than the course diagram and more likely to survive an ordinary week. She asked Tian to knock if a collector arrived while she was resting, and Tian agreed for those particular afternoons.

lantern_08_061.speaker: narrator
lantern_08_061.text: Outside, Han Tao's brother walked past with the patched bird. He had tied a second line to keep it from reaching the baker's open fire, but the extra restraint made the bird turn awkwardly. Yue watched him adjust the length while his sister waited with the empty baskets. He tried again after the first change failed and kept the second knot visible.

lantern_08_062.speaker: narrator
lantern_08_062.text: That freedom was stranger than she had expected. A woman from Lower Glass recognized her and asked why an afternoon message had waited. Yue directed her to Hou, who held the current received records, and offered to walk with her to the office. She did not reconstruct a private case from memory beside the food stall. The woman accepted the walk and complained about the weather on the way. Once inside, she obtained the case's actual delay explanation. She left annoyed about the delay rather than about being treated as a nuisance.

lantern_08_063.speaker: narrator
lantern_08_063.text: Yue spent that night finishing a sheet whose child author described a lamp at a ferry stop. The child had written that it made the dark shorter. He Pu's correction changed the wording to a more technical description of visibility. Yue wanted to preserve the child's sentence. She marked a query and waited for the editor rather than silently restoring it. The next day he read both versions aloud and chose the original. The agreed copy followed that received decision. Work could contain judgment without permitting every participant to declare herself its final owner.

lantern_08_064.speaker: narrator
lantern_08_064.text: The postponed fourth live appointment would occur after this interval, under the same six-appointment extension; its cells and inspections had not been consumed by the cancellation. Four appointments had taken place, one dry and three live, with their following checks. The accepted six-cell stock had supplied three live sessions, leaving three for the named later work rather than an unlimited collection of retries. Yue could state what remained without spending the night recounting it. Her next morning needed sleep more than another beautifully ruled inventory.

lantern_08_065.speaker: narrator
lantern_08_065.text: Before putting out her room's ordinary oil lamp, she reread the route plan once. It now contained a missing portion, an interrupted breath, a moved date, and a correction that looked untidy beside her first elegant drawing. These marks were the useful part. Across the lane someone was singing the chorus that had lost a verse at the concert. Yue listened until the tune ended, then went to bed. Her capacity remained her measured stage-eight capacity. The person learning how to use it had acquired several more reasons to stop, and several more reasons to begin.
